recipes.title: Shoyu ramen with soft eggs
recipes.blurb: Soy-ginger chicken broth, springy noodles, jammy eggs

steps.text: Bring the broth, soy sauce, mirin, garlic and ginger to a simmer in a large pot.
Add the chicken thighs and simmer gently until they reach 165°F.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs in a separate pot for 6 minutes 30 seconds, then chill in ice water.
Peel and halve the eggs. Lift out the chicken, rest it, then slice thinly.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water until just tender, then drain well.
Divide noodles into bowls and ladle hot strained broth over them.
Top with chicken, eggs, green onions and a drop of sesame oil.

recipes.title: Miso ramen with pork and corn
recipes.blurb: Rich miso broth, ground pork, sweet corn and butter

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork until cooked through (160°F).
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and bring to a simmer. Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth, then stir it back in.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Keep the broth just below a boil.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot until tender, then drain.
Divide the noodles and corn into bowls. Ladle in the hot broth and pork.
Top each bowl with butter and green onions.

recipes.title: Yaki udon
recipes.blurb: Stir-fried udon with chicken, cabbage and a savory sauce

steps.text: Loosen the udon in hot water for 1 minute, then drain.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and oyster sauce together in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken until browned and 165°F.
Add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry until softened.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss until everything is hot and glossy.
Fold in the green onions and top with bonito flakes.

recipes.title: Yakisoba
recipes.blurb: Street-food stir-fried noodles with pork and cabbage

steps.text: Stir the Worcestershire, ketchup, soy sauce and sugar together to make the sauce.
Microwave or steam the noodles 1 minute, then loosen them with your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the pork until browned and 145°F.
Add the onion, carrot and cabbage and stir-fry until crisp-tender.
Add the noodles and sauce. Toss until coated and hot.
Serve topped with pickled red ginger.

recipes.title: Zaru soba
recipes.blurb: Chilled buckwheat noodles with a dipping sauce

steps.text: Simmer the water, dashi powder, soy sauce and mirin for 2 minutes, then chill until cold.
Boil the soba in plenty of water until tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles under cold running water, rubbing gently to remove starch.
Cut the nori into thin strips with scissors.
Pile the noodles on plates and top with nori and sesame seeds.
Serve with the dipping sauce, green onions and wasabi on the side.

recipes.title: Kitsune udon
recipes.blurb: Udon in light dashi broth with sweet fried tofu

steps.text: Bring the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a simmer.
Add the fried tofu and simmer gently so it soaks up the broth.
Boil the udon in a separate pot until warmed through, then drain.
Divide the noodles into four deep bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles and place 2 tofu pouches on each bowl.
Sprinkle with green onions.

recipes.title: Spicy sesame ramen
recipes.blurb: Tantanmen-style bowl with sesame-chili broth

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil in a pot over medium-high heat until cooked through (160°F).
Add the garlic, ginger and chili garlic sauce and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth, tahini, soy sauce and vinegar. Whisk and simmer until smooth.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot, adding the bok choy for the last minute. Drain.
Divide noodles and bok choy into bowls.
Ladle the broth and pork over the top and finish with green onions.

recipes.title: Hiyashi chuka
recipes.blurb: Cold ramen salad with ham, egg and cucumber

steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and water until the sugar dissolves. Chill.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and cook thin omelets in the oil in a nonstick skillet.
Roll the omelets and slice into thin ribbons.
Boil the noodles until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Arrange the noodles on plates with cucumber, tomato, ham and egg in sections.
Pour the sauce over the top and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Curry udon
recipes.blurb: Thick Japanese curry broth over chewy udon

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the meat and cook until no longer pink (pork 145°F).
Add the water and dashi powder and bring to a simmer.
Turn off the heat, add the roux blocks and stir until melted. Simmer until thick.
Stir in the soy sauce.
Boil the udon in a separate pot, then drain and divide into bowls.
Pour the curry over the noodles and top with green onions.

recipes.title: Butter corn ramen
recipes.blurb: Sapporo-style bowl with sweet corn and a pat of butter

steps.text: Simmer the broth with the garlic and soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth, then stir it into the pot.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot until tender, then drain.
Warm the corn in the broth for the last 2 minutes.
Divide the noodles into bowls and ladle in the broth and corn.
Top each bowl with 1 tbsp butter and green onions.

recipes.title: Gyudon beef bowl
recipes.blurb: Thin-sliced beef and onion simmered sweet-savory over rice

ingredients.item: thinly sliced beef ribeye or sirloin

steps.text: Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Keep it warm.
Combine the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger in a wide pan and bring to a simmer.
Add the onions and simmer until soft.
Add the beef, separating the slices, and simmer until no longer pink.
Spoon rice into bowls and top with beef, onions and a little sauce.
Finish with pickled ginger and green onions.

recipes.title: Oyakodon
recipes.blurb: Chicken and egg simmered in sweet dashi over rice

steps.text: Cook the rice according to the package and keep it warm.
Simmer the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide skillet.
Add the onion and chicken and simmer until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Pour the eggs over the chicken in a circle. Cover and cook until just set but still soft.
Scoop the rice into four bowls.
Slide the chicken and egg over the rice and top with green onions.

recipes.title: Katsudon
recipes.blurb: Crispy pork cutlet simmered with egg over rice

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin chops (about 5 oz each)

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Pound the chops thin, season with salt and black pepper, then coat in flour, egg and panko.
Heat the oil in a skillet to 350°F. Fry the cutlets until golden and 145°F inside, about 3 minutes per side.
Slice the cutlets into strips.
Simmer the onion with the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin and sugar until soft.
Lay the cutlets on the onions, pour the beaten eggs over, cover and cook until just set.
Slide the topping over bowls of hot rice.

recipes.title: Soboro don
recipes.blurb: Three-color bowl of ground chicken, scrambled egg and greens

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Combine the chicken, soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger in a pan. Cook over medium heat, stirring into fine crumbles, to 165°F.
Beat the eggs with 1 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt. Scramble over low heat into small curds.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water, squeeze dry and chop.
Toss the spinach with the sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Serve rice topped with rows of chicken, egg and spinach.

recipes.title: Chicken katsu curry rice
recipes.blurb: Crispy chicken cutlet with mild Japanese curry sauce

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Add the carrots, potatoes and water and simmer until tender.
Turn off the heat, stir in the roux until melted, then simmer until thick.
Season the chicken with salt, then coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry the chicken in 350°F oil until golden and 165°F, about 3 minutes per side.
Slice the cutlets and serve over rice with the curry.

recipes.title: Butadon pork bowl
recipes.blurb: Honey-soy glazed pork and onions over rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, ginger and garlic together.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the pork and cook until browned and 145°F.
Pour in the sauce and cook until it thickens into a glaze.
Serve over rice with green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Salmon avocado donburi
recipes.blurb: Pan-seared salmon, avocado and soy-sesame dressing on rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil and sugar for the dressing.
Pat the salmon dry and season with salt. Sear in the oil over medium-high heat, 3 to 4 minutes per side, to 145°F.
Flake the salmon into large pieces.
Divide the rice into bowls and add salmon, avocado and cucumber.
Drizzle with the dressing and top with nori and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Japanese vegetable curry rice
recipes.blurb: Mild, thick curry with potato, carrot and onion

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Cook the onions in the oil in a large pot until golden.
Add the carrots, potatoes, mushrooms and water. Cover and simmer until tender.
Turn off the heat, add the roux blocks and stir until melted.
Stir in the grated apple and simmer until thick.
Serve the curry over rice.

recipes.title: Hayashi rice
recipes.blurb: Beef and mushroom stew in a rich tomato-demi sauce

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Melt the butter in a pot. Brown the onions and mushrooms over medium-high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Add the wine, broth, ketchup, Worcestershire and soy sauce.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve over rice.

recipes.title: Chicken teriyaki
recipes.blurb: Pan-seared thighs glazed in a glossy homemade teriyaki sauce

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger together. Mix the cornstarch with the water.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken skin side down until browned, about 6 minutes.
Flip and cook until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Pour in the sauce and the cornstarch mix. Simmer, turning the chicken, until glossy.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.
Top with sesame seeds and green onions.

recipes.title: Salmon teriyaki
recipes.blurb: Quick pan-seared salmon with a sticky teriyaki glaze

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger together.
Pat the salmon dry and season lightly with salt.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the salmon skin side up for 4 minutes.
Flip and cook 3 minutes more, to 145°F inside.
Pour the sauce into the pan and simmer, spooning it over the salmon, until thick.
Serve topped with green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Chicken yakitori skewers
recipes.blurb: Grilled chicken and green onion skewers with tare glaze

steps.text: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and water until reduced by one third to make the tare.
Thread chicken and green onion pieces alternately onto the soaked skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Grill the skewers, turning, for 6 minutes.
Brush with tare and grill, turning, until the chicken is glazed and 165°F.
Brush once more with tare before serving.

recipes.title: Tsukune chicken meatballs
recipes.blurb: Tender chicken meatballs glazed in sweet soy

steps.text: Mix the chicken, green onions, panko, egg, ginger and 1 tbsp soy sauce until sticky.
Wet your hands and shape into 16 small meatballs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs all over, then cover and cook to 165°F.
Stir the remaining soy sauce, mirin, sugar and water together.
Pour into the pan and roll the meatballs until glazed.
Serve warm, with rice or on skewers.

recipes.title: Pork shogayaki
recipes.blurb: Thin pork sautéed in a ginger-soy sauce

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger together in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the pork and cook until browned and 145°F.
Pour in the sauce and cook until it coats the pork.
Serve over the shredded cabbage.

recipes.title: Miso-glazed salmon
recipes.blurb: Sweet white miso glaze broiled until caramelized

steps.text: Heat the broiler with the rack 6 inches from the heat. Line a pan with foil.
Mix the miso, mirin, soy sauce, sugar and ginger into a paste.
Spread the paste over the salmon and place on the pan.
Broil until caramelized and the salmon reaches 145°F.
Rest for 2 minutes and top with green onions.

recipes.title: Yakiniku beef
recipes.blurb: Grilled marinated steak slices with a sweet-soy dip

steps.text: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, sesame oil, garlic and half the green onions.
Toss the beef with two thirds of the sauce and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or skillet until very hot and brush with the oil.
Grill the beef in batches, about 1 minute per side, until browned.
Serve with the remaining sauce for dipping, sesame seeds and green onions.

recipes.title: Hambagu steak
recipes.blurb: Juicy Japanese-style hamburger steak with a ketchup sauce

steps.text: Soak the panko in the milk. Sauté the onion in a little oil until soft and let it cool.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, panko, egg, salt and black pepper until sticky.
Form four oval patties and press a dimple into the center of each.
Cook in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes per side, then cover for 5 minutes until 160°F.
Remove the patties. Add the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and water to the pan and simmer 2 minutes.
Spoon the sauce over the patties.

recipes.title: Teriyaki tofu steaks
recipes.blurb: Crisp pan-seared tofu in a glossy teriyaki glaze

steps.text: Press the tofu with paper towels for 10 minutes, then cut each block into 4 slabs.
Pat dry and dust the slabs with cornstarch.
Pan-fry in the oil over medium-high heat until golden, about 4 minutes per side.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, ginger and garlic together and pour into the pan.
Simmer, turning the tofu, until the sauce thickens.
Top with green onions.

recipes.title: Tonkatsu
recipes.blurb: Crisp panko pork cutlets with tangy tonkatsu sauce

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin chops (about 5 oz each)

steps.text: Make the sauce by stirring the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar together.
Pound the chops to 1/2 inch thick. Season with salt and black pepper.
Coat each chop in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing firmly.
Heat the oil to 350°F in a large skillet. Fry the chops until golden and 145°F inside.
Drain on a rack and rest for 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
Serve over shredded cabbage with the sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken katsu
recipes.blurb: Golden panko chicken breast cutlets

steps.text: Mix the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar for the sauce.
Pound the chicken to an even 1/2 inch and season with salt and black pepper.
Coat the cutlets in flour, then egg, then panko.
Heat the oil to 350°F in a large skillet. Fry until golden and 165°F inside, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on a rack, slice and serve with the sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken karaage
recipes.blurb: Japanese fried chicken marinated in ginger and soy

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, mirin, ginger and garlic. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 340°F.
Coat the chicken in the potato starch, shaking off extra.
Fry in batches until golden, about 5 minutes. Chicken must reach 165°F.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Shrimp tempura
recipes.blurb: Light crisp shrimp with a dipping sauce

steps.text: Simmer the water, soy sauce and mirin for 1 minute, then add the ginger. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Score the shrimp bellies and straighten them. Pat dry.
Quickly whisk the flour, cornstarch, sparkling water and egg. Leave it lumpy.
Dip the shrimp in batter and fry until pale gold, about 2 minutes. Shrimp must reach 145°F.
Drain on a rack and serve right away with the dip.

recipes.title: Vegetable tempura
recipes.blurb: Crisp sweet potato, green beans and mushrooms in light batter

steps.text: Simmer the water, soy sauce and mirin for 1 minute for the dip.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch and sparkling water just until mixed. Lumps are fine.
Dip the vegetables in batter and fry in small batches until crisp, 3 to 4 minutes.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with salt.
Serve at once with the dip.

recipes.title: Ebi fry
recipes.blurb: Panko-crusted fried shrimp with tartar-style sauce

steps.text: Hard-boil the egg 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop.
Mix the mayonnaise, pickles, lemon juice and chopped egg to make the sauce.
Pat the shrimp dry, season with salt, and coat in flour, egg and panko.
Heat the oil to 350°F. Fry the shrimp until golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Shrimp must reach 145°F.
Drain on a rack and serve with the sauce.

recipes.title: Korokke potato croquettes
recipes.blurb: Crunchy croquettes filled with potato and beef

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until very tender, then drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp oil, then add the beef, soy sauce and sugar. Cook to 160°F.
Fold the filling into the mash and cool until easy to handle.
Shape into 12 ovals. Coat in flour, egg, then panko.
Heat the oil to 350°F. Fry the croquettes until deep golden, about 3 minutes.
Drain on a rack and serve warm.

recipes.title: Agedashi tofu
recipes.blurb: Crispy tofu cubes in warm savory dashi

steps.text: Press the tofu with paper towels for 10 minutes and cut into 8 cubes.
Simmer the water, dashi powder, soy sauce and mirin for 3 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry and coat lightly in starch.
Fry in 350°F oil until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes.
Place the tofu in shallow bowls and pour the hot broth around it.
Top with green onions and ginger.

recipes.title: Chicken nanban
recipes.blurb: Fried chicken in sweet-sour sauce with tartar sauce

steps.text: Hard-boil an egg for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop. Mix with the mayonnaise and pickles for tartar sauce.
Simmer the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar for 2 minutes. Pour into a shallow dish.
Season the chicken with salt, dust with flour and dip in beaten egg.
Fry in 350°F oil until golden and 165°F inside, about 6 minutes.
Roll the hot chicken in the sauce, then slice.
Serve with the tartar sauce.

recipes.title: Miso soup with tofu and wakame
recipes.blurb: Classic everyday soup in 15 minutes

steps.text: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the water and dashi powder to a gentle simmer.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth, then stir it in.
Do not let it boil. Serve topped with green onions.

recipes.title: Tonjiru pork miso soup
recipes.blurb: Hearty miso soup with pork, root vegetables and tofu

ingredients.item: thinly sliced pork belly or shoulder

steps.text: Cook the pork in the sesame oil in a pot until it loses its pink color.
Add the carrot, daikon, potato, water and dashi powder. Simmer until tender.
Add the tofu and heat through.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth and stir it in. Do not boil.
Serve topped with green onions.

recipes.title: Clear mushroom soup
recipes.blurb: Light soy-dashi broth with mushrooms and spinach

steps.text: Bring the water and dashi powder to a simmer.
Add the soy sauce, mirin and mushrooms. Simmer until tender.
Add the spinach and cook 30 seconds until wilted.
Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.
Serve with a little grated ginger on top.

recipes.title: Egg drop soup (kakitamajiru)
recipes.blurb: Silky eggs ribboned through hot savory dashi

steps.text: Bring the water, dashi powder, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer.
Mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water and stir it in until the soup thickens slightly.
Slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring gently.
Turn off the heat once ribbons form.
Add a pinch of salt and serve with green onions.

recipes.title: Japanese sweet corn soup
recipes.blurb: Creamy, sweet corn potage like a Japanese bakery

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion until soft.
Add the cream-style corn, frozen corn, water and bouillon. Simmer.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender or in batches.
Stir in the milk and sugar and warm gently.
Season with salt and black pepper.

recipes.title: Shabu-shabu
recipes.blurb: Swish paper-thin beef and vegetables in simmering broth

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Put the water and kombu in a pot on the table. Bring to a simmer and remove the kombu.
Arrange the beef and vegetables on platters.
Add the hard vegetables and tofu first and simmer until tender.
Swish each beef slice in the broth until just gray, about 10 seconds. Beef must be cooked through.
Dip in ponzu or sesame sauce and eat with rice.

recipes.title: Sukiyaki
recipes.blurb: Sweet soy beef hot pot with tofu, noodles and vegetables

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and water together to make the warishita.
Rinse and drain the shirataki noodles.
Heat a wide pan on the table and pour in half the sauce.
Add the beef, tofu, mushrooms, noodles and vegetables in sections and simmer until cooked.
Add more sauce as needed.
Dip the hot beef into a bowl of beaten egg and eat.

recipes.title: Chicken mizutaki hot pot
recipes.blurb: Gentle chicken and vegetable nabe with ponzu

steps.text: Put the chicken, water and kombu in a large pot. Bring to a gentle simmer, removing the kombu when bubbles form.
Skim the foam and simmer the chicken until it reaches 165°F.
Add the carrots and cabbage stems and simmer.
Add the mushrooms, tofu, cabbage leaves and green onions. Cook until tender.
Serve from the pot with ponzu for dipping.

recipes.title: Simple oden
recipes.blurb: Daikon, eggs and fish cakes simmered in light dashi

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs 10 minutes, cool and peel.
Bring the water, dashi powder, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a wide pot.
Add the daikon and simmer until tender.
Add the eggs, fish cake and konnyaku and simmer gently.
Let it stand 10 minutes so flavors soak in.
Serve with a dab of mustard.

recipes.title: Pan-fried gyoza
recipes.blurb: Crisp-bottomed pork and cabbage dumplings

steps.text: Mix the pork, cabbage, green onions, garlic, ginger, 1 tbsp soy sauce and sesame oil.
Put 1 tsp filling in each wrapper, wet the edge, fold and pleat to seal.
Heat the vegetable oil in a nonstick skillet. Arrange gyoza flat side down and brown 2 minutes.
Add the water, cover and steam until the pork reaches 160°F.
Uncover and cook until the water is gone and the bottoms are crisp.
Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce with the vinegar for dipping.

recipes.title: Salted edamame
recipes.blurb: The easiest snack: steamed pods with flaky salt

steps.text: Bring a pot of water to a boil with 1 tbsp salt.
Add the frozen edamame and cook until bright green and tender.
Drain well and shake dry.
Toss with the sesame oil and sea salt.
Serve warm and squeeze the beans out of the pods.

recipes.title: Tamagoyaki rolled omelet
recipes.blurb: Layered sweet egg roll for bento or breakfast

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, mirin, soy sauce and water until even.
Heat a small nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and oil it lightly with a paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer of egg. When nearly set, roll it up to one end.
Oil the pan, pour in more egg under the roll, and roll again. Repeat until all the egg is used.
Rest the omelet 2 minutes, then slice into pieces.

recipes.title: Onigiri rice balls
recipes.blurb: Salted rice triangles with a salmon filling

steps.text: Cook the rice and let it cool until warm enough to handle.
Mix the salmon with the mayonnaise and soy sauce.
Wet your hands and rub them with salt.
Press a small handful of rice flat, add 1 tbsp filling and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori.

recipes.title: California rolls
recipes.blurb: Crab, avocado and cucumber rolls with rice outside

steps.text: Rinse the rice, cook with the water, then rest covered 10 minutes.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Fold into the rice and cool.
Cover a bamboo mat in plastic wrap. Spread rice on half a nori sheet, sprinkle with sesame and flip.
Lay crab, avocado and cucumber along the nori edge.
Roll tightly with the mat and press to seal.
Cut each roll into 8 pieces with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce.

recipes.title: Cucumber sunomono
recipes.blurb: Cool, tangy cucumber salad with sesame

steps.text: Toss the sliced cucumbers with the salt and let sit for 10 minutes.
Whisk the vinegar, sugar and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Squeeze the cucumbers firmly to remove water.
Toss with the dressing and chill until ready.
Top with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Spinach gomae
recipes.blurb: Blanched spinach in sweet sesame dressing

steps.text: Boil a large pot of water and blanch the spinach until wilted.
Plunge into ice water, then squeeze dry and cut in 2-inch pieces.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar or spice grinder until crushed.
Stir the sugar, soy sauce and mirin into the sesame.
Toss with the spinach and serve cool.

recipes.title: Chirashi sushi bowl
recipes.blurb: Seasoned rice topped with salmon, egg and vegetables

steps.text: Rinse the rice, cook with the water, then rest covered 10 minutes.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved, fold into the rice and let cool.
Beat the eggs and cook in a thin layer in a nonstick pan. Slice into ribbons.
Cut the fish into thin pieces. If using shrimp, boil until pink and 145°F.
Divide the rice into bowls and arrange the toppings on top.
Garnish with nori and serve with soy sauce and wasabi.

recipes.title: Okonomiyaki
recipes.blurb: Savory cabbage pancakes with sauce and mayo

steps.text: Whisk the flour, water, dashi powder and eggs into a batter. Fold in the cabbage and green onions.
Mix the Worcestershire and ketchup for the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Pour in half the batter and top with bacon.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and cook until the bacon is crisp and the center is set.
Repeat with the rest of the oil and batter.
Brush with the sauce and drizzle with mayonnaise.
